ingredients.item: pork shoulder or collar, sliced 4 mm against the grain
/2 Asian pear , grated, juice included here — this lane wants the juice
/2 tsp black pepper ; 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
Steamed rice , lettuce ssam, ssamjang , kimchi , gyeran mari rolled omelet for the kids' plate

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Medium-high fire, single loose layer, sixty to ninety seconds undisturbed. The wet marinade wants a hiss, not a roar — if it boils gray in its own liquid, the pan is crowded; lift half the batch off and do two rounds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the slices take color at the edges while the marinade caramelizes on the pan behind them — the smell is sweet soy and pork fat, and the pan should be building a glossy brown film, not a watery boil.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip at the beading edge, 60–90 seconds more, pull while the centers still shine. Scrape the pan's caramelized juice into a small bowl as you go — over rice is where it lands.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: test piece: sweet-savory edge, juicy interior, no heat anywhere — the register should be round and gentle, with the pear as a perfume rather than a flavor.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Platter, sesame over; the bowl route (rice, juice, slices) and the ssam route both open.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the rice bowl test: the juice should be glossy brown and spoonable, milder than the marinade tasted raw — if it is syrupy-sweet, pull the honey back a tablespoon next batch.

visualDonenessCues: the slices take color at the edges while the marinade caramelizes on the pan behind them — the smell is sweet soy and pork fat, and the pan should be building a glossy brown film, not a watery boil.
test piece: sweet-savory edge, juicy interior, no heat anywhere — the register should be round and gentle, with the pear as a perfume rather than a flavor.
the rice bowl test: the juice should be glossy brown and spoonable, milder than the marinade tasted raw — if it is syrupy-sweet, pull the honey back a tablespoon next batch.
storageNotes: Marinated pork keeps 24 hours. Cooked, 3 days — leftover ganjang bulgogi over cold rice with a fried egg and a spoon of the reserved juice is the lunchbox move.
Variations: the spicy fork (#M13); add gochugaru by the half-teaspoon to walk this lane toward the heat gently; chicken thigh takes the same marinade (#M16).
